question: Which of these common grains naturally contains gluten?
explanation: Barley is one of the main grains that naturally contains gluten, along with wheat and rye. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h1)

question: What is gluten's main job when baking bread and pastries?

options.A: It acts as a primary artificial sweetener
options.B: It preserves food against bacterial spoilage
options.C: It gives dough elasticity and chewy texture
options.D: It adds essential vitamin C to baked goods

explanation: Think of gluten as the stretchy protein network that traps gases, giving bread its lovely bounce and structure! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h1)

question: What happens inside the small intestine of someone with celiac disease when they eat gluten?

options.D: Villi are damaged and flatten out

explanation: When gluten triggers an immune reaction in celiac disease, the tiny finger-like villi that absorb nutrients get flattened out. Great nursing insight to remember! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h2)

question: How is a wheat allergy different from celiac disease?

options.A: Wheat allergy involves IgE antibody responses rather than autoimmune villous atrophy
options.B: Celiac disease symptoms only appear after age fifty
options.C: Wheat allergy causes permanent damage to the liver instead of the gut
options.D: Celiac disease is caused by a bacterial infection of the stomach

explanation: A wheat allergy is a classic immune system allergic reaction (using IgE antibodies), whereas celiac disease is an autoimmune condition that specifically harms the gut lining. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h2)

question: Which of these grains is naturally safe to eat on a gluten-free diet?
explanation: Quinoa is a fantastic pseudocereal that is naturally free of gluten. Perfect for safe and healthy meal planning! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h3)

question: A patient asks if fresh eggs and plain milk are okay on a gluten-free diet. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only if they are labeled with a special certification stamp.
options.B: Dairy is allowed, but eggs must be strictly avoided.
options.C: Yes, fresh eggs and plain dairy are naturally free of gluten.
options.D: No, all animal products contain traces of wheat protein.

explanation: Pure, unprocessed whole foods like eggs, meat, and plain milk do not contain gluten naturally. Simple and safe! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h3)

question: Why does soy sauce often catch beginners off guard as a hidden source of gluten?

options.A: Soybeans naturally cross-pollinate with wheat plants in the field.
options.B: Manufacturers add wheat flour to soy sauce as an artificial coloring agent.
options.C: Traditional soy sauce is brewed using fermented wheat alongside soybeans.
options.D: Soy sauce undergoes chemical processing that creates synthetic gluten.

explanation: Surprise! Most commercial soy sauces use wheat as a key ingredient during brewing. Always check those labels! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h4)

question: Which of these common drinks must be avoided on a gluten-free diet?
explanation: Since standard beer is brewed from barley, it is packed with gluten unless marked specifically as gluten-free. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h4)

question: What is a common nutrition mistake people make when switching to packaged gluten-free foods?

options.A: Consuming too much natural protein from fresh fruits and vegetables
options.B: Eating too many processed substitutes lacking fiber and B vitamins
options.C: Developing an immediate intolerance to all dairy products
options.D: Suffering from severe protein toxicity due to meat overconsumption

explanation: It's easy to rely on packaged gluten-free snacks, but many lack the fiber and vitamins found in whole or fortified foods. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h5)

question: Which nutrient is most often missing in unfortified gluten-free grain alternatives?
explanation: Standard wheat products are usually fortified with B vitamins like folate, which alternative flours often lack unless added back. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h5)

question: What does cross-contamination mean when keeping a diet gluten-free?

options.A: Safe food coming into physical contact with gluten-containing surfaces or utensils
options.B: The natural mutation of gluten proteins inside harvested grains
options.C: The chemical breakdown of proteins during high-heat baking
options.D: Mixing different types of safe gluten-free grains in one storage container

explanation: Cross-contamination happens when tiny bits of gluten accidentally transfer from a dirty counter, knife, or pan onto a safe meal. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h6)

question: Which kitchen tool is notorious for trapping wheat crumbs and causing cross-contamination?

options.A: Stainless steel pots used for boiling water
options.B: Toasters used for regular wheat bread
options.C: Ceramic dinner plates washed in hot water
options.D: Glass storage bowls with tight plastic lids

explanation: Toasters hold onto bread crumbs inside their heating coils, making them nearly impossible to clean completely for someone with celiac disease. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h6)

question: A patient newly diagnosed with celiac disease is stressed about grocery shopping. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Advise the patient to avoid eating all packaged foods forever.
options.B: Refer the patient immediately to a psychiatric inpatient facility.
options.C: Provide a strict list of expensive specialty imported commercial snacks.
options.D: Teach the patient how to identify naturally gluten-free whole foods and read labels.

explanation: Empowering patients with label-reading skills and showing them naturally safe whole foods builds confidence and reduces anxiety! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h7)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients managing celiac disease?

options.A: Mental stress directly converts into physical gluten proteins inside the gut.
options.B: Patients usually develop severe memory loss from carbohydrate withdrawal.
options.C: Strict dietary restriction and social isolation can create significant emotional distress.
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only proven cure for intestinal villous atrophy.

explanation: Living with a lifelong, rigid diet can feel isolating and stressful. Being a warm, supportive nurse makes all the difference for their mental well-being! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h7)
